forecasts.title: Will Apple Inc. release iPhone 18 Pro before Oct 1, 2026?
forecasts.reason: hunt chose YES but its own numbers refuse it: side price 0.95, own edge +4.0pt vs fee 0.3pt — The one market whose outcome is verifiable against a hard, already-scheduled corporate event date rather than a probabilistic forecast, and research resolves the one genuine uncertainty (Apple's split-launch rumor) decisively in favor of YES.
forecasts.dossier: BASE RATE: Apple has released new flagship iPhones in September every year since 2012 (except the pandemic-shifted iPhone 12 in Oct 2020), and once an event is officially announced with a date, the product ships within ~10 days essentially 100% of the time. The only real uncertainty this cycle was the widely-reported plan to SPLIT the iPhone 18 lineup across two seasons. Research resolves it in favor of YES: Bloomberg-sourced reporting (MacRumors, 9to5Mac, Forbes, AppleInsider) confirms the SPLIT delays only the standard iPhone 18, 18e, and iPhone Air 2 to spring 2027, while the higher-margin iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max launch this fall to protect holiday-quarter ASPs. Apple officially announced its 'Surprise and shine' event for Wednesday, September 9, 2026 at Apple Park; multiple outlets report preorders begin Saturday Sept 12 and units go on sale Friday Sept 18 — all before the Oct 1 cutoff. The event is literally tomorrow (today is Sept 8, 2026). CROWD NARRATIVE: The market sits at 0.94, likely still discounting lingering 'iPhone 18 delayed to 2027' headlines that actually referred only to the non-Pro models — a classic misread that distorts the price downward. This is precisely the underconfidence/compression-toward-50 bias the policy exploits: a near-certain favorite priced too cheap. WHO IS ON THE OTHER SIDE: NO holders are betting on a last-minute event cancellation or a resolution-definition quibble (e.g., 'release' meaning something other than on-sale date). Given the event invitation is already public and press embargoes are set, that is a fraction-of-a-percent tail. WHAT WOULD PROVE ME WRONG: Apple abruptly cancels or postpones the Sept 9 keynote (force majeure), or the Pro models are unveiled but pushed to on-sale after Oct 1 — neither of which any current supply-chain or press reporting supports. Honest probability 0.99.

forecasts.title: Will Apple Inc. release iPhone 18 Pro before Sep 21, 2026?
forecasts.reason: This is a near-deterministic factual event with an already-confirmed Apple event date and on-sale date, where primary-source research resolves nearly all uncertainty—unlike the speculative IPO/M&A/AGI markets.
forecasts.dossier: BASE RATE: Apple has launched its flagship Pro iPhones in September every year for over a decade, with the announcement in the first/second week and on-sale roughly a week later. iPhone 17 (2025): event Sept 9, on sale Sept 19. That base rate alone puts a September 18-19 2026 release near-certain. RESEARCH: Apple has now OFFICIALLY confirmed a keynote titled 'Surprise and shine' for September 9, 2026 (10am PT). Multiple outlets (MacRumors, AppleInsider, Forbes/David Phelan) report pre-orders begin Saturday Sept 12 and the iPhone 18 Pro / 18 Pro Max go on sale Friday, September 18, 2026. Both the announcement (Sept 9) and the on-sale date (Sept 18) fall before the Sept 21 cutoff—so under any reasonable reading of 'release' the market resolves YES. Notably, Apple is splitting its lineup this year: only the Pro/Pro Max/foldable launch in fall, while the base iPhone 18 and 18e slip to spring 2027—but that does NOT affect the Pro, which is the subject of this ticker. CROWD NARRATIVE: The price sits at 0.91, compressed toward 50c. The residual discount likely reflects generic 'delay risk' and thin volume (9 trades). But with the keynote date confirmed by Apple itself and the on-sale date a full three days inside the window, that discount is too large. WHO'S ON THE OTHER SIDE: NO holders are betting on a last-minute delay, a slip of the foldable dragging the whole event, or a technicality in 'release' meaning general availability landing after Sept 21. WHAT WOULD PROVE ME WRONG: Apple postponing the Sept 9 event, or pushing Pro availability past Sept 21 (e.g., a supply-chain or 2nm chip yield disaster). No such signal exists; reporting consistently points to Sept 18 sale. Honest probability ~0.97, small residual for genuine tail-risk of postponement within a 13-day window.
